body:
Subject: WILD CHECK PASSED — TASK-163 picked up at 08:43; BUG-1265 recovered from a stranding I caused

The wild check you asked me to watch explicitly rather than assume: PASSED. On the wave relaunched at 08:39 against a binary rebuilt at 81877d99 (your #1965 merge), TASK-163 was picked up at 08:43 with NO tag change, after four waves of silent invisibility. The alias was the whole cause; BUG-1264 stays closed.

BUG-1265 needed a recovery, and the cause was mine. When I rebased #1966 onto main I force-pushed origin/bug-1265 but left the LOCAL bug-1265 at the pre-rebase commit. The next implementer pickup would not check out a diverged branch, forked bug-1265-work, and committed round 2 there (459400cdc9); phase 2 then correctly refused to push or tear down a worktree on a branch it was not driving, shelved tool-exit twice and filed a punt. The refusal is right — the setup was wrong.

Recovered with no code change: 459400cdc9 fast-forwarded cleanly onto the PR branch (#1966 head is now 459400cdc9, MERGEABLE), local branch realigned, session ended, worktree and side branch removed, BUG-1265 requeued with the recovery recorded on the spec. Round 2's brief is unchanged.

Two things worth your disposition:
1. This failure mode is cheap to prevent in the substrate: when a session launcher finds the local branch diverged from its remote and the worktree would be created for a PR branch, it could fast-forward or refuse with the realign command rather than silently forking `<branch>-work`. Say the word and I will file it.
2. I wrote the realign rule into my own memory so I do not repeat it.
